# Cluster Reference

## How jobs are submitted

`sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh` starts the launcher job. Inside it, Snakemake uses
`snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm` to submit each rule as its own SLURM job.

## Compute sites

Everything specific to a compute site lives in one folder under `profiles/`.
The config, test config and samplesheet are the same on every cluster.

| Folder | For |
|--------|-----|
| `profiles/longleaf/` | UNC Longleaf (SLURM) |
| `profiles/pioneer/` | Case Western Pioneer (SLURM) |
| `profiles/slurm-template/` | Any other SLURM cluster: copy and fill in the `<...>` values |
| `profiles/local/` | One machine with no scheduler (a workstation, or an interactive GPU node) |

Each folder has two files:

- `env.sh`: sourced by `ChromSimPipe.sh` and `unlock.sh`; makes `python3`
  (≥ 3.11) and `conda` available (`module load ...`, or
  `source ~/miniforge3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh`).
- `config.yaml`: the Snakemake profile: scheduler, account, partitions, and
  each rule's CPUs / memory / GPU.

To set up a new SLURM cluster:

```bash
cp -r profiles/slurm-template profiles/<cluster>
nano profiles/<cluster>/config.yaml   # account, CPU partition, GPU partition (+ QOS if required)
nano profiles/<cluster>/env.sh        # module loads for python3 and conda
echo 'export CHROMSIM_PROFILE=profiles/<cluster>' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh
```

`sinfo -s` lists partitions, `sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER` lists your
accounts, and `module avail` shows the available software.
`--profile profiles/<cluster>` picks a site for a single run. For
`profiles/local`, start with `bash ChromSimPipe.sh` instead of `sbatch`.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Profile status.** The test config (then 9 jobs, polychrom engine) has run end to end on Longleaf
(GPU simulation included). On Pioneer the test has completed the CTCF steps
(identical to Longleaf's), the GPU simulation (V100) and the merge. Run the
test config on any new cluster first.
:::

### Per-cluster settings

Three things differ between clusters. All are set once per cluster and stay
out of git, so the same config and samplesheet run everywhere:

| Setting | How | Used by |
|---------|-----|---------|
| Compute profile | `export CHROMSIM_PROFILE=profiles/<cluster>` in `~/.bashrc` | `ChromSimPipe.sh`, `unlock.sh` |
| Output location | `export CHROMSIM_OUTPUT_ROOT=/path/to/scratch/ChromSimPipe` in `~/.bashrc` | every rule (via `configs/parameters.py`) and the launcher's SLURM log folder |
| Input files | symbolic links in `data/` named as in the samplesheet | the samplesheet and `genome` |

The profile is chosen by `--profile`, then `$CHROMSIM_PROFILE`, then
`hpcProfile` in the config (default `profiles/longleaf`). A relative
`outputDir` goes under `$CHROMSIM_OUTPUT_ROOT`, or under the repo folder if
it is unset; an absolute `outputDir` is used as written. SLURM jobs inherit
the environment of the shell that ran `sbatch`, so open a new shell (or
`source ~/.bashrc`) after editing it. Linking the inputs is described in
`data/README.md`.

On Pioneer, inputs and code live in home and compute output goes to scratch:

| What | Where |
|------|-------|
| Peaks, `.hic` maps, genome FASTA | a folder in home, linked into `data/` |
| The clone (and the conda environments Snakemake builds inside it) | home |
| Miniforge | `$HOME/miniforge3` |
| Output (simulations, analysis, logs) | scratch, via `CHROMSIM_OUTPUT_ROOT` |

```bash
cat >> ~/.bashrc <<'EOS'
export CHROMSIM_PROFILE=profiles/pioneer
export CHROMSIM_OUTPUT_ROOT=/scratch/pioneer/users/$USER/ChromSimPipe
EOS
source ~/.bashrc
```

Scratch is purged automatically, so copy `<outputDir>/analysis/` and
`<outputDir>/*_benchmarking.tsv` back to home when a run finishes.

## Pioneer (Case Western)

| Setting | Value | Where |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Account | `pjt5_1` (its QOS `gpuext2` applies by default) | `default-resources: slurm_account` |
| CPU partition | `batch` | `default-resources: slurm_partition` |
| GPU partition | `gpu` (39 nodes, 114 GPUs), requested as `gpu: 1` (`--gpus=1`) | `set-resources: simulateShard` |
| Software | your own Miniforge (Pioneer's `Miniconda3` modules ship conda 23.x) | `env.sh` |

## SLURM account and partition (Longleaf)

All of these are in `profiles/longleaf/config.yaml`:

| Setting | Value | Where |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Account | `rc_dphansti_pi` | `default-resources: slurm_account` |
| Default partition | `general` | `default-resources: slurm_partition` |
| GPU partitions | `l40-gpu,volta-gpu,gpu` (first with a free node) | `set-resources: simulateShard` |
| GPU QOS | `gpu_access` | `set-resources: simulateShard` |

`env.sh` activates your own Miniforge (see [Conda](#conda-version) below):
Longleaf's `anaconda` modules ship conda 24.1, older than Snakemake needs.

## Per-rule resource requests

| Rule | Partition | CPUs | RAM | Wall time | GPU |
|------|-----------|------|-----|-----------|-----|
| `convertHic` | general | 4 | 32 GB | 8 h | - |
| `getMotif` | general | 1 | 1 GB | 15 min | - |
| `orientCTCF` | general | 2 | 16 GB | 1 h | - |
| `validateCTCF` | general | 1 | 4 GB | 15 min | - |
| `preparePolysim` (engine: polysim only) | general | 1 | 4 GB | 30 min | - |
| `simulateShard` | **l40-gpu, volta-gpu, gpu** | 4 | 60 GB | 12 h | **1** |
| `mergeShards` | general | 4 | 64 GB | 2 h | - |
| `analyzeCondition` | general | 4 | 64 GB | 24 h | - |
| `benchmarkSummary` | general | 1 | 2 GB | 15 min | - |

## Log file locations

| Log | Path |
|-----|------|
| Launcher (main Snakemake process) | `ChromSimPipe-{jobid}.out` |
| Each job's stdout / stderr | `<outputDir>/logs/{rule}_{wildcards}.out` / `.err` |
| SLURM job logs | `<outputDir>/logs_slurm/` (`--slurm-logdir` in `ChromSimPipe.sh`) |
| Per-job run time / memory | `<outputDir>/benchmarks/`, summarised in `<outputDir>/{runName}_benchmarking.tsv` |

`<outputDir>` is `output/` (or `output_test/`) in the repo folder, or under
`$CHROMSIM_OUTPUT_ROOT` when that is set.

## Conda version {#conda-version}

Snakemake 8.27 requires conda 24.7.1 or newer and stops with
`Conda must be version 24.7.1 or later` otherwise. Neither Longleaf's
`anaconda` modules (24.1) nor Pioneer's `Miniconda3` modules (23.x) are new
enough, so both profiles use a Miniforge you install once per cluster:

```bash
wget https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh
bash Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh -b -p $HOME/miniforge3
rm -rf env        # the launcher's venv, if it was built with another Python
```

`env.sh` activates it (set `CHROMSIM_CONDA_ROOT` to use another location).
The rule environments themselves are built inside the repo
(`.snakemake/conda/`), so keep the clone on storage that is not purged.

## Conda environments in SLURM jobs

Each rule declares `conda:` with an entry from `condaEnvs` in the config, and
the profile sets `software-deployment-method: conda`. Snakemake activates the
environment inside each job. The site's `env.sh` puts `conda` on the `PATH`
that SLURM jobs inherit. Rules run scripts with `"$CONDA_PREFIX/bin/python"`,
the activated environment's own interpreter, because in cluster jobs another
`python` (for example the launcher's `env/` venv) can come first on `PATH`.

### Resource values in profiles

Snakemake evaluates each resource value as a Python expression. Numbers and
bare words work (`gpu: 1`, `qos: gpu_access`), but text with punctuation needs
an inner pair of quotes: `gres: "'gpu:1'"`, not `gres: "gpu:1"`. A dry run does
not catch this; the error appears when the job is submitted.

### Measured run times (Longleaf, test config)

| Step | Wall time | Peak memory |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| `convertHic` (3.7 GB `.hic`) | 1 h 37 min | 3.5 GB |
| `simulateShard` (1,000 blocks, 1 GPU) | 2 min 48 s | 0.5 GB |
| `mergeShards` | 42 s | 0.2 GB |
| `analyzeCondition` | 6 min 31 s | 2.0 GB |

A full-run shard is 12,500 blocks, so roughly 35 min on the same GPU type.

In the full Longleaf run (3 replicates × 50,000 blocks per condition), shards
took about 1 h each on `l40-gpu` and `volta-gpu`. `analyzeCondition` took about
4.5 h for two conditions; the third ran past 6 h after SLURM placed it on the
`spill` partition, hence the 24 h limit.

## Checking queue status

```bash
squeue -u $USER                   # all your jobs
squeue -u $USER -t R              # only running jobs
squeue -j <jobid>                 # specific job
sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,ExitCode
```

## Cancelling jobs

```bash
scancel <jobid>                   # one job
scancel -u $USER                  # ALL your jobs (careful!)
scancel -u $USER --name <jobname>        # by job name
```

After cancelling, run `bash unlock.sh` before resubmitting.

## Legacy cluster scripts

The standalone SLURM batch scripts from before Snakemake was adopted were
written for the lab's original cluster and now live in `legacy/cluster/`.
They are preserved for reference but should not be used.
`sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh` is the current entry point for everything.
